High catalyst experiment separated things somewhat. M16 is now best, followed by M17, M12, M14, M20, M11, M9 - all deactivation mechanisms! The baseline M1, M2, M13, M18, M19 are ~1 unit worse, while M6, M8, M7 are also worse. This suggests some deactivation is occurring. Need to distinguish what kind of deactivation: cat-based (M9), S-based (M11, M16), P-based (M12, M17), or catS-based (M14, M20).

<hypothesis>
To distinguish deactivation types, I need an experiment where substrate and product concentrations create different scenarios:
- **Low substrate** suppresses catS formation, so catS-based deactivation (M14, M16, M17, M18, M20) slows relative to cat-based (M9) or S+cat (M11)
- **High product with low substrate**: tests M12 (P+cat) and M17 (P+catS) but now [catS] is low
- **High substrate, low catalyst, long time**: maximizes catS, amplifies M14, M16, M17, M18, M20

The most discriminating experiment: **high substrate (3.0 M), low catalyst (0.005 M), no product**. This:
- Runs slowly, gives long time window to see late-stage deactivation
- High [S] pushes equilibrium to catS, enhancing catS-based deactivation (M14, M16, M17, M18, M20) vs free-cat deactivation (M9, M11, M12)
- Low [cat] suppresses dimer pathways (M2, M13, M19)
- High [S] enhances M11 (S+cat deactivation) and M16 (S+catS)
- Should distinguish M9 (simple decay) from M11, M14, M16 (concentration-dependent)
</hypothesis>
